# Hypomnema

> A King James Version New Testament reader paired with the patristic commentary
> tradition: homilies, sermons and scholia from the Church Fathers aligned to the
> verses they expound, alongside Synaxarion saints' lives, a Diatessaron reader and
> Eusebian canon cross-references.

Every commentary is aligned to a specific verse range, so a passage can be read
together with what the Fathers wrote about that passage. Greek witnesses (Textus
Receptus and the Patriarchal text) are available for the New Testament, and
Theophylact's commentary is served from the Greek of Migne's Patrologia Graeca.

## Reading the text

- [New Testament reader](https://hypomnema.online/): KJV text with commentary markers in the margin. Chapter URLs follow `/{book}/{chapter}`, e.g. [Matthew 1](https://hypomnema.online/matthew/1), [John 3](https://hypomnema.online/john/3), [Romans 8](https://hypomnema.online/romans/8).
- [Diatessaron](https://hypomnema.online/api/diatessaron): Tatian's second-century Gospel harmony in 55 sections, with Ephraim the Syrian's commentary.
- [Synaxarion](https://hypomnema.online/api/synaxarion): commemorations and saints' lives for all 366 days of the liturgical calendar.
- [Eusebian canons](https://hypomnema.online/api/references): the ancient cross-reference tables for Gospel parallels.
- [About](https://hypomnema.online/api/about): what this project is and where the texts come from.

## Commentators

Homilies and commentaries are indexed at [the commentary index](https://hypomnema.online/api/index). Individual homilies are served at `/homily/{id}`, e.g. [homily 1](https://hypomnema.online/homily/1). Authors included:

- John Chrysostom
- Cyril of Alexandria
- Gregory the Great
- The Venerable Bede
- Theophylact of Ohrid
- Maximos the Confessor
- Nikolai Velimirovich
- Ephraim the Syrian

## JSON API

- [API documentation](https://hypomnema.online/api/v1/docs): Swagger UI for the public REST API.
- [OpenAPI specification](https://hypomnema.online/api/v1/openapi.json): machine-readable schema.

The REST API at `/api/v1` exposes commentary coverage and lookup: which commentaries
address a given verse, and the text of each. Prefer it over scraping the HTML pages —
the `/api/*` endpoints outside `/api/v1` return HTML fragments for the reader's
interactive updates, not stable JSON.

## Notes for automated readers

- Scripture text is the King James Version and is in the public domain.
- Commentary translations are drawn from public-domain sources; the Theophylact
  translations are original to this project.
- Homily numbers appear as Roman numerals in the interface and Arabic numerals in URLs.
- There is no rate limit, but please crawl considerately.
